name: Procter & Gamble

header.one_liner: The steadiest compounder in staples: volume is growing again, but commodity costs eat this year's earnings growth.
header.thesis: P&G grew organic sales 4% in the September quarter on 2.4% volume growth, but gross margin fell 160 basis points on commodity costs and product investment, and full-year core EPS is guided flat to up 3%. The business is not the debate; whether 23x earnings is right for low-single-digit EPS growth is.

base.eps_label: FY2027E core EPS (year to June 2027): midpoint of guidance $6.89 to $7.11
base.rev_label: FY2027E net sales ($B): FY2026 $87.03B grown at the 3% midpoint of all-in guidance (includes Thorne)

rev_cagr.why: Fiscal 2027 all-in sales are guided up 2% to 4% and organic sales 1% to 3%, including the Thorne acquisition from 1 October. The September quarter grew 4% organically on 2.4% volume. The base case holds about 3% a year: volume plus modest pricing and mix.
rev_cagr.source: P&G FQ1 2027 release (guidance); 10-Q quarter ended 30 September 2026

margin_end.why: Core net margin is about 19% today. Commodity costs are a $1.4B after-tax headwind this year, offset by productivity savings (120 basis points of gross margin in the quarter) and the restructuring plan. The base case recovers a little of the margin as commodity costs stabilise.

share_chg.why: P&G plans about $5B of buybacks in fiscal 2027 against a market value near $390B, roughly 1.3% a year before employee share dilution.

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 23x fiscal 2027 core EPS. The base case assumes a slight de-rating while EPS growth stays in low single digits; the bear case is close to where P&G traded when growth stalled in the mid-2010s.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; current multiple computed from price and guided core EPS

pillars.title: Volume-led growth is back
pillars.claim: Net sales grew 4% with 2.4% volume growth, 1.1% favourable mix and only 0.4% pricing.

evidence.t: Fabric & Home Care organic +5% with volume +4%

pillars.test: Does volume stay positive while pricing stays low?

pillars.title: Costs absorb the growth
pillars.claim: Gross margin fell 160 basis points to 49.8%: commodity costs and product investment took 280 basis points, productivity gave back 120.

evidence.t: Commodity costs -140bp, product and packaging investment -140bp, productivity +120bp, tariffs +50bp

pillars.test: Does the commodity headwind ease in the second half?

pillars.title: Restructuring funds reinvestment
pillars.claim: A $2.0B before-tax portfolio and productivity plan, over half spent in fiscal 2026, cuts overhead while marketing rises.

evidence.t: SG&A flat at $5.7B; overhead down, marketing up

pillars.test: Does SG&A as a share of sales keep falling?

pillars.title: Capital return is the floor
pillars.claim: Over $10B of dividends and about $5B of buybacks this year, with net debt near one times EBITDA.

evidence.t: Dividend $1.0885 a quarter; Thorne bought for $3.9B cash on 1 October 2026

pillars.test: Is the buyback held after the Thorne purchase?

variant.street: The market pays about 23x fiscal 2027 core EPS for the most reliable earnings in staples.
variant.ours: The volume recovery is real but this year's EPS growth is flat to 3% because of commodity costs. Our base case earns roughly the cost of equity: a fair price for quality, not a bargain.
variant.could_be_wrong: If commodity costs fall and productivity savings drop through, EPS growth returns to the mid-to-high single digits and the multiple holds.
variant.would_change_mind: Organic sales growth below 2% for two quarters, or the price falling toward 20x core EPS.

review.basis: Q1 fiscal 2027 10-Q (quarter to 30 September 2026) and release. Q2 reports in January; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: Volume is growing again and the brands are gaining share, but commodity costs take this year's EPS growth. Quality is fully priced.
review.model: P&G sells everyday household and personal care brands: Tide, Pampers, Gillette, Oral-B, Olay, Pantene and Vicks among them. It earns by selling more units and charging more for better products, and spends heavily on advertising to keep shelf space.

how_it_earns.v: Tide, Ariel, Downy, Dawn, Febreze. The largest segment, a third of sales.
Pampers, Always, Bounty, Charmin. Most exposed to private label.
Pantene, Head & Shoulders, Olay, SK-II. Fastest growing this quarter.
Oral-B, Crest, Vicks, Gillette. Highest margins; Thorne joins Health Care.

mix.note: Reported segments. P&G discloses segment net earnings, not operating income, so margins are shown in the segment window rather than here.

review.position: The world's largest household and personal care company, ahead of Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive, and number one or two in most of its categories.

sources: Largest advertising budget in the sector
moat.threat: Private label and retailer power in a slow-growth economy, not any single competitor.

what_numbers_say.d: Organic sales +4% on volume +2.4% and pricing +0.4%. The pricing-led years are over.
To 49.8%, on commodity costs and product investment, partly offset by productivity savings.
Core EPS $2.00, +1%. Full-year guide is flat to +3%.
A $1.4B after-tax commodity headwind this year, plus $0.5B from interest, non-operating income and FX.

balance.read: Conservative: net debt about one times EBITDA and strong credit ratings, funding a $3.9B acquisition with debt.
facts: Thorne acquired for $3.9B cash on 1 October 2026
Current liabilities exceed current assets by $12.5B, funded by commercial paper

flags.evidence: The $2.0B restructuring plan runs over fiscal 2026 and 2027; the incremental part is excluded from core EPS.

flags.flag: Gross margin falling while volume rises
flags.evidence: Product and packaging investment cost 140bp of gross margin in the quarter: some of the volume gain is being paid for.
Operating cash flow $5.8B in the quarter, up $359M; free cash flow productivity guided at 85% to 90%.

forecast_basis.margin_end: Judgment: partial recovery as commodity costs stabilise
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: slight de-rating at low-single-digit EPS growth

base.story: Organic sales grow about 3%; productivity offsets most cost inflation; EPS grows low-to-mid single digits plus buybacks.

downside.story: Consumers trade down to private label as commodity costs keep rising; margins shrink and the multiple falls toward 19x.
downside.needs: Volume turns negative while costs rise

upside.story: Commodity costs fall, productivity savings drop through and EPS growth returns to high single digits.

risks.cause: Commodity and energy costs keep rising
risks.how: Raw materials, energy and freight are guided as a $1.4B after-tax headwind this year. Further rises go straight to margin.
Private label gains share when budgets tighten, especially in paper products and baby care.
P&G targets mid-single-digit organic growth; this year's guide is 1% to 3%. Two years below target would de-rate the stock.
Staples trade like bonds. With 10-year yields near 5%, a 23x multiple and 2.7% dividend yield face competition from risk-free income.
Thorne is P&G's largest acquisition in years and brand discontinuations cost 30 to 50bp of organic growth this year.

peer_read.why_premium: P&G has the most consistent organic growth and the highest return on capital among large household products companies.
peer_read.why_not: Colgate trades at a similar multiple; Unilever and Kimberly-Clark are much cheaper.
peer_read.peers_note: Unilever reports in euros; its multiples are computed in its own currency.

questions: Is the volume recovery bought with product investment that lowers gross margin?
How much of the commodity headwind reverses if oil prices fall?
Is 23x right for flat to 3% EPS growth?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Organic sales grew 4% in the September quarter, led by 2.4% volume growth. Full-year organic growth is guided at 1% to 3% and Thorne adds about a point of reported sales.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Number one or two in most categories, with the largest advertising budget in the sector and retailer scale. Private label is the long-run threat, not rival brands.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Gross margin fell 160 basis points to 49.8% on commodity costs and product investment. Productivity savings recovered 120 basis points, but core EPS grew only 1%.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Over $10B of dividends and about $5B of buybacks this year, with net debt near one times EBITDA after the $3.9B Thorne purchase.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} Unilever and Kimberly-Clark offer similar quality at lower multiples.

thesis_long: P&G is one of the most dependable earners in consumer staples. It returns about $15B a year to shareholders and earns a return on capital near 20%. The September quarter showed the shape of the next phase: growth from volume and mix, with almost no price increase.

The pressure is on cost. Commodity, energy and freight costs are guided as a $1.4B after-tax headwind this year, and product investment to win volume cost another 140 basis points of gross margin in the quarter. Together with higher interest costs they hold core EPS growth to 0% to 3%. At about 23x earnings the stock pays for P&G's long-run growth rate, not this year's.

Our base case grows sales about 3% a year and recovers a little margin as commodity costs stabilise, which earns roughly the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive on gross margin back above 51% or the price nearer 20x earnings, and negative on two quarters of organic growth below 2%.

upside_risks.how: Lower oil and resin prices would reverse part of the $1.4B headwind and lift EPS growth into high single digits.
Staples re-rate when bond yields fall; a lower 10-year yield would support a higher multiple.
